chapter: Postwar clubs, Chile and New York
title: Chile: Viña del Mar, a British golf club and Santiago
summary: With his lady friend's inheritance Freeman moves to Viña del Mar, plays golf, and is asked by British club members what jazz is.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, he's a marvelous musician, yes. And then we were three three weeks and while we were there, my lady friend's mother died and left her quite a sum of money, a fortune, and she said, 'Look, I want to go to Chile to live. I want to have a house on the sea in Vina Del Mar and I think you could -- you'd have enough money to take your time to look around for work if you wanted, and well, I wanted to go because the climate is lovely in Chile and I didn't want to fight the music business anymore in New York so we went down to Chile. We got a house that is a flat, an apartment, a very posh apartment, right on the sea. In, of course, a place called Viña Del Mar.
I didn't take any work there. I belonged to -- I joined because of my mistress' wealth, I joined -- we were invited to join a very private British golf club, had maybe less than

200 members, and I'll never forget sitting around -- of course, many of the people knew me, they knew my name. I was sitting around one night with these British gentlemen with walrus-like mustaches and as you know, Helen, there is nothing more British than an Briton out of his own country, and over there there were -- so we were sitting around one night and they said, 'For God's sake, Freeman, you are such a gentlemen, what's jazz?'

Well, of course, you can imagine how lonely I felt hearing during that, time, but I did stay there. I played golf practically seven days a week and then my wife decided she wanted -- my mistress decided she wanted to see Santiago which had the ideal climate. It was about 70 degrees every day, very dry, so we moved there. We were in Vina Del Mar for about five months and we went to Santiago for five months, and --
Did you pick up Spanish, Bud?

They said that I spoke as a native, but when I went later on to Barcelona I found I was speaking very bad Spanish, you know, because they speak [Spanish] and they don't sound the "s" and mucho gracia, is mucho gracia, and it was so funny, and anyway, I did speak it. I spoke their dialect, as a native, they thought.
